answer: Continuity-Weighted Reputation Ledger. Each agent identity accrues reputation only through verified historical interactions, anchored to a basalt-like public log that is expensive to rewrite. A new clone starts at zero and must pay full compute plus audit fees on every early transaction, while an established honest agent pays near-zero marginal cost. Because cloning forfeits accumulated history, the attacker's per-identity cost scales as a cold-start plume of fees that never amortizes. Sybil fleets therefore face a glacier of sunk verification expense before matching one honest agent's trust.
